clue.text: A river abroad

definitions.meaning: a Scottish waterway that runs past Stirling into a firth near Edinburgh
in its old sense, out and away from home, onwards

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions side by side; the OCR dropped the r of 'river'.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense names a Scottish waterway; the other is an archaic adverb meaning outwards, away from home, which is what 'abroad' once meant.

clue.text: Wanting to travel some distance South, into Cornish town

parts.note: a foot is a short distance

indicators.note: south goes into the town's name

parts.note: Looe is a fishing town in Cornwall, in south-west England

explanation.surface: A restless traveller heads some way south into a town in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: Footloose means free of ties and so inclined to roam.

clue.text: Call to attention soldiers, foot and mounted

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means raised up, so the soldiers' letters are read upwards

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Infantry and cavalry are ordered to stand to attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldiers supply RE twice: once as they stand, once 'mounted', i.e. turned upwards to ER, making a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer a matter is to bring it to someone's notice.

clue.text: Dance with spirit — it's child's play

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
Scotch is whisky, a spirit

explanation.surface: Dancing after a dram is easy, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a playground game children play by hopping between chalked squares.

clue.text: Anticipate using wood before everything

indicators.note: the wood comes before everything, so its synonym is placed first

parts.note: a wood is a forest
everything is all

explanation.surface: Someone gets ahead of a rival by exploiting woodland first.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to act in advance so as to prevent something, i.e. to get in first.

clue.text: Quite a distance, of course

definitions.meaning: on a golf course, the mown stretch between tee and green

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means a good long way; as one it is the golf term for the main mown strip of each hole.

clue.text: Soldier's uniform

definitions.meaning: a member of the permanent professional army

explanation.definitionFit: A regular is a full-time professional soldier, and as an adjective it means steady and unvarying.

clue.text: Hoax upsetting? Dandies love being taken in

indicators.note: love is taken into the reversed dandies, going inside them
in a down clue, upsetting turns the word upside down so it reads backwards

parts.note: fops are dandies
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A prank: dandies are fooled about love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns FOPS into SPOF, and 'being taken in' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoof is a trick or a parody meant to fool people.

clue.text: The wealth of a crook with internal complaint

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the complaint is internal to the crook, so it sits inside

parts.note: a fence is a criminal who receives stolen goods
flu, influenza, is an illness

explanation.surface: A rich villain suffers from a stomach upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' reads as a grievance but is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluence means riches or abundance of money.

clue.text: Under cover you are, they say, sensational

indicators.note: the spoken words go under the cover, so they sit within it

parts.note: a lid is a cover

indicators.note: signals the words are taken as heard rather than spelt

parts.note: said aloud it sounds like the letters U R

explanation.surface: Someone is told their secret undercover work is sensational.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under cover' looks like a phrase for secret agents; 'Under' is the container signal, and 'they say' marks the spoken letters standing for 'you are'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid means shocking and luridly vivid, as in a gaudy sensational story.

clue.text: Descendants well off, to start with

indicators.note: says the word off comes at the start, ahead of the synonym for well

parts.note: taken as written
a spring is a natural well or source of water

explanation.surface: The rich heirs began life comfortably off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well off' reads as 'wealthy', but 'well' is the water source and 'off' stands as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are children, the people descended from a parent.

clue.text: Present officer in charge has deserted

indicators.note: the abbreviation for in charge leaves the word officer, like a deserter quitting his post

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A serving officer in command has gone absent without leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like an adjective about the officer; it is the verb, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To present something is to put it forward for acceptance, which is to tender it.

clue.text: Cyril's rewritten the words

indicators.note: the letters of Cyril are written again in a new order

parts.note: the possessive 's is no letter, leaving the name Cyril

explanation.surface: Cyril has produced a fresh draft of the text.
explanation.definitionFit: A song's lyric is its text, the verse set to music.

clue.text: Having everything necessary, we will begin

parts.note: contracted to we'll
to found something is to start it up

explanation.surface: A team announces it will start once it is fully equipped.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-found ship or house is fully fitted out and supplied with all it needs.

clue.text: Stop too long where in France saint drowned in river

parts.note: the French for where is où

indicators.note: the saint is plunged inside the river, so its letters go within

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river

explanation.surface: A tourist in France lingers at the spot where a saint drowned.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstay is to remain beyond the proper time, as in overstaying a welcome.

clue.text: Going, in a slow stream to deceive the fish

parts.note: to trick is to deceive
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An angler moves slowly down a stream in order to fool the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Trickling describes liquid moving in a thin, slow flow.

clue.text: Following _ about point one recurring

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: running back on itself, so the word for one is read backwards

parts.note: a unit is one
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: A maths lesson on the decimal nought point one recurring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point one recurring' looks like the decimal 0.1 with a repeating digit; 'recurring' is the reversal signal, and the pieces join in answer order, not clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the band of attendants who follow an important person; following as a noun means a body of supporters.

clue.text: Staff employed by the police

parts.note: reads as personnel on the force payroll, but staff means a stick

explanation.surface: A note on people who work for the constabulary.
explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is the short club carried by a British police officer.

clue.text: Let me lean out of the weather

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so these letters are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks to step indoors out of the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemental describes the forces of nature such as wind and rain, the elements.

clue.text: Record in it the description

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: read as 'in it, the': the word the sits inside it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to note down the description in it.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is a descriptive word or phrase attached to a name, like 'the Great'.

clue.text: Initiators of train robbery serve hard labour

indicators.note: the initial letters of the two words

parts.note: to avail is to be of use, to serve

explanation.surface: The ringleaders of a train robbery are sentenced to hard labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail means toil or painful effort.

clue.text: Concoction they use to get some sleep

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture cooked up, so these letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A sleeping draught that people take to help them nod off.
explanation.definitionFit: Shut-eye is informal for a nap or a spell of slumber.

clue.text: He rests in a permanent way

definitions.meaning: permanent way is the British term for railway track; the timber beams lie in it

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a person dozing and a timber beam supporting rails on a railway track.

clue.text: Come about to accept the position

parts.note: to take is to accept
a place is a position

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to take up the post being offered.
explanation.definitionFit: To take place is to happen or occur.

clue.text: Shy boy, I would

parts.note: Tim is a boy's name
contracted to I'd

explanation.surface: A bashful lad says he'd like to.
explanation.definitionFit: Timid means lacking confidence, nervous of others.

clue.text: court the girl I love

parts.note: Pat is a girl's name
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A suitor woos the girl he loves.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved open courtyard beside a house.

clue.text: A length of rope

definitions.meaning: a nautical measure, a tenth of a sea mile
a thick strong rope such as an anchor hawser

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a sailors' unit of distance of about 200 yards and a heavy hawser.

clue.text: The wind is raised — a pound, then fourteen

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are lifted to read upwards

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight
a stone, st, is fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A balloon goes up as weights of a pound and then fourteen are dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' is a reversal signal in a down clue and turns only 'a pound'; the stone of fourteen pounds then follows unturned.
explanation.definitionFit: A blast is a strong gust of air.

clue.text: Starting second finish first, sweating a bit

indicators.note: the word for second goes at the start, with the word for first at the finish

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
1st, with the numeral 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A racer who started in second place finishes first, barely breaking sweat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finish' places 1ST at the end; the stray quotation mark is an OCR artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist means slightly damp, as skin is when perspiring lightly.

clue.text: Booth upset when plans are ruined

definitions.text: Booth upset when plans are ruined

parts.words: Booth upset when plans are ruined
parts.note: a fruit seller's stall tipped over is the idiom for spoiling a scheme

explanation.surface: A market stall is knocked over and someone's plans fall apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset the apple-cart is the idiom for wrecking an arrangement, and the cart is a fruit seller's stall.

clue.text: Used to dress the cloth

parts.note: the cloth is the clergy; the clue reads as tailoring but means what priests wear at the neck

explanation.surface: A tailor describes what a piece of fabric was cut for.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-collar is the stiff white band worn by clergy, who are called the cloth.

clue.text: Land of one's birth

definitions.meaning: a former province of South Africa
relating to the place or time someone was born

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the South African province, now KwaZulu-Natal; the other is the adjective meaning connected with being born.
